svg.title: RA-001 Figure 4 — Logical Assurance Architecture for Cross-Organizational Pharmaceutical Traceability
svg.desc: Vendor-neutral logical assurance architecture preserving authoritative operational and regulatory systems across six logical layers, four assurance dimensions, cross-cutting evidence protection and trust lifecycle governance, and conditional mechanism selection.
svg.text: Vendor-neutral logical model — existing authoritative systems remain authoritative
Boundary assurance overlays strengthen cross-organizational evidence without requiring replacement of existing systems of record.
• Partner and jurisdiction-specific systems of record
• GTIN • Serial • Lot / Batch • Expiry • SSCC
• Manufacturing / Packaging → Logistics → Distribution / Wholesale → Dispensing → Patient
• Physical possession, custody, condition and handover context
Integrity • signatures • hashes • provenance • protected evidence
Trust anchors • policy • credential status • key lifecycle • audit
• Verified / sufficiently supported for the applicable workflow
• Quarantine, investigation, escalation or other applicable operational
PKI, signatures, credentials, trusted directories, append-only
evidence, federated verification and shared-ledger mechanisms are
candidates selected according to the assurance boundary and use
Event integrity ≠ physical truth • Credential verification ≠ transaction authorization • Device identity ≠ calibration • Immutable history ≠ correctness

Source: KryoNex Research synthesis informed by GS1 EPCIS/CBV, U.S. FDA DSCSA, EU medicines-verification requirements, Indian pharmaceutical traceability frameworks, and evaluated assurance mechanisms.
